earth.what: Chorus radio waves in Earth's magnetic field, recorded by NASA's Van Allen Probes (EMFISIS) and turned into sound

jupiter.what: Waves in the charged gas near Jupiter, detected by NASA's Cassini as it flew past in 2001, turned into sound

saturn.what: Saturn's radio emissions linked to its auroras, recorded by Cassini and turned into sound

mars.what: Real wind on Mars, recorded by the microphone on NASA's Perseverance rover on 20 Feb 2021

moon.what: Apollo 11, 20 July 1969: "Houston, Tranquility Base here. The Eagle has landed."

enceladus.what: Radio and plasma waves near Enceladus recorded by NASA's Cassini, turned into sound

launch.what: NASA's SLS rocket launching Artemis II, 1 April 2026, recorded at Pad Camera Site 4

sun.what: The Sun's real vibrations: 40 days of SOHO's Michelson Doppler Imager data, sped up 42,000 times so we can hear them
sun.credit: ESA/NASA SOHO · A. Kosovichev, Stanford Experimental Physics Lab · NASA

mercury.what: An artist's sound for Mercury: solar-wind crackle on a world with almost no air (not a recording)

venus.what: A natural radio signal from Venus' upper atmosphere, picked up by NASA's Parker Solar Probe flying past Venus on 11 July 2020, turned into sound
venus.credit: NASA/GSFC Scientific Visualization Studio · Glyn Collinson

uranus.what: Plasma waves around Uranus, recorded by Voyager 2 on 24 January 1986, the only spacecraft ever to visit Uranus
uranus.credit: NASA Voyager 2 Plasma Wave Science · The University of Iowa
uranus.license: Courtesy of NASA and The University of Iowa (space-audio.org, CC BY 4.0)

neptune.what: An artist's sound for Neptune, home of the fastest winds in the Solar System (not a recording)

pluto.what: An artist's sound for faraway, frozen Pluto (not a recording)
